problem: Loop Engine software changes can pass checked transitions without an inspectable record of which review obligations exist or whether external review occurred. A fresh actor resuming a run cannot reliably distinguish a reviewed change from a vacuous allow.
outcome: Runs using a shipped software-change profile expose frozen review obligations and refuse each configured checked transition until its artifact is structurally valid and external evidence satisfies every configured axis.
acceptance: A caller can inspect the frozen policies and artifact schemas before evaluating a transition.
A malformed subject artifact is denied with each violated rule named before semantic evidence is considered.
Current-revision evidence from distinct non-subject authors is required for every configured axis.
The reference workflow reaches its terminal state only after its configured validation obligations are satisfied.
constraints: The engine owns workflow progress while external actors own review judgment and authored work.
Policies and schemas are immutable run input; provider code must not embed their content.
The reference topology remains unchanged and the provider remains a fresh-process, local subprocess.
non_goals: Provider-side semantic judging or model invocation.
New workflow states, transitions, or mid-run waiver support.
Cryptographic provenance, content hashing, or locking of authored artifacts.
Standalone installed packaging beyond the repository-local reference distribution.
